items.title: Earl Foster Interview
items.q: There's an old picture that Edmund Hall, the clarinetist, he's in New York now. ... I don't think Edmund was in the band at the time. ... I don't think he was a member of the band, was he?

ctx.x: Oh yeah, listen boy, we forget after this fellow, Louis Kepard. We must never forget Buddy Mallory. Yeah. And the Arnold was on too. He went and lived over there. He's from right here, right downtown, right in the district, you know. Buddy. He played with him a long time. That's who came with him. During the time when I came with him, Buddy Mallory came with him. Oh yeah. Because he and this boy, I don't know if something happened. The lawyer was supposed to go play with Celestine, see. Anyway, he got this boy…

We played with Armstrong different people a few years ago. But Edmund Hall had this picture, I think, of the band across the lake with Buddy Petit and Mandeville. And I forget my word about that. Mandalay, I mean. No, Buddy Mallory, that's a guitar player. Yeah.

items.title: Earl Foster Interview
items.q: Count Hall, he may have been on that picture, I don't know. I don't think he was playing the band in the study acting.

ctx.x: We missed, by the way we never did interview him yet, we ought to interview him pretty soon. Somehow we missed him, somehow we never did get to him.

Yeah, I think he has a picture of it. He told me, he has a picture of the band, you know, of the old things. Yeah, but he has a picture of it. Now, Count Hall, he may have been on that picture, I don't know. I don't think he was playing the band in the study acting. Well, I thought Edmund Hall was on that picture. I mean Edmund Hall, I mean Edmund Hall, I mean Edmund Hall, that's what I mean. It may be Edmund Hall if you don't think it's Fritz. Well, I… Fritz played with him, Edmund Hall was playing with the…
